pr_comments:
Sure, no problem :sweat_smile: :+1:  
Thanks a lot for the update.
(I have kept the code logical per commit, so it should be easy and faster reviewing on a commit-by-commit basis)
Any updates? Its been quite a few weeks :sweat_smile:

@AliabbasMerchant similar apologies as for your other PR: this work got caught by the vortex of our codebase refactor. Are you up for getting this work reconciled with trunk? I think that this testing might actually have become easier as you can now put a template finding helper (for both issue and pr create) into the factory that is passed to commands and inject it in tests.

Okay. Cool. No issues.

I kindof lost track amidst the refactoring wave, but hope to resume contributions, seeing that the refactoring part is done, and we are now again open to accept community contributions. :ok_hand: 

Will do this in 2-3 days and will re-request a review then.

thanks for your patience and understanding, @AliabbasMerchant !

that refactor was sorely needed and there was no elegant way to balance it against incoming PRs. But yes, it's done now; there is still plenty of cleanup we could do but in terms of fundamental changes we don't have anything planned.

@AliabbasMerchant Thank you! Would you be up to consider a potentially simpler avenue of approaching this? The new command structure might make it easier to stub out the current directory in tests, which we could use to point a command to a fixed location on disk where the fixtures for templates reside. That way you wouldn't have to introduce a whole mechanism for mocking template results, and we could keep the diff at minimum. Let me know if you'd like me to sketch out what I had in mind! 🙇

@mislav Sure. I am planning to do this today. (Sorry for the delay)  
Will first go through the changes in the command structure, and will definitely keep your suggestions in mind. :+1:

I went through the refactored code - Great job! The code looks much cleaner and is more manageable :heart:  

As @mislav suggested, there is no longer a need for this mocking mechanism, and so this PR is kinda unneeded. Hence, am closing this and have opened #1582 instead.

issue_context.title: make template selection test-able
issue_context.body:
We don't currently have the ability to test template selection during issue/pr creation and we
should.
comments: Also, we need tests for interactive mode in issue/pr creation

Can I take up the tests for the interactive mode?  
I tried it out locally, and the tests I wrote are working.

I can later on try stubbing the template file selection also

Got the solution!  
I feel we actually don't need to *exactly* stub the template file selection.
(Your comments here: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4d11732a474fb4651704f9d9876d9f627e4283b5/command/issue.go#L362 and here: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4d11732a474fb4651704f9d9876d9f627e4283b5/command/pr_create.go#L218)
What I think is, instead of stubbing and putting demo files in the flow, we can actually utilize the existing template files in the flow.  
Let `gh` select our existing issue and pr templates from the file system, and then when the user selects that particular option of the template, we can directly check if the contents are proper.
(And we don't need to check for the change due to the user opening the text editor, as that is the job of the `surveyext` library, and we can assume that it is well tested.)
Also, we already have `github_template_test.go` for template content extraction stuff testing.

In case I was unable to put forth my ideas clearly, I believe that I will be able to show it better via a PR. (and commenting on my changes there)
sure, if you are up to it! Let me know if you have any questions or difficulties with the `AskStubber` and `CommandStubber` helpers.
oop, page was out of date. I'm happy to look at a PR and discuss there. Thanks for thinking about it and for checking in! Assign me as a reviewer, please.

review_comments: This is for setting up the `cobra.Command` and the `args []string`, to be directly passed to our functions, so that we can invoke them directly, without relying on cobra to do that.

IMO, We can use this trick to stub anything.  
No need to create extra command-specific structs, and build them here and pass them to the command, to be read there.  
All that is internally handled by cobra here.
The handler with the proper working; to be used when not testing.
I unexported these, so that we don't use them directly by mistake, and are reminded to use the handler.
I hope I have covered all major cases/formats here.
